name: bussin
blurb: Really good, especially delicious food: "this burger is bussin"
title: Bussin Meaning: What Does Bussin Mean in Slang?
description: Bussin means really good, especially delicious food. From African American English, it was defined on Urban Dictionary in 2017 and spread on TikTok in 2020–21.
answer: Bussin (often written bussin') means extremely good, and most of all delicious: "these wings are bussin" means they taste amazing. The word comes from African American English, probably from "busting" or "bursting" (as in bursting with flavour), and was defined on Urban Dictionary in December 2017. It took off on social media in 2020 and spread widely on TikTok in 2021, and now it can describe anything great, not just food.

body: The core meaning is food that tastes amazing. Dictionaries define it as "great, wonderful, amazing" or "extremely good", with Wiktionary marking "delicious" as the original sense and "really good" as an extension.
The spelling shows how it is said: "bussin" drops the t and the g of "busting", the way people talk in casual African American English. The apostrophe in bussin' marks the dropped g.

head: Date
Event
rows: Dictionary.com dates the first recorded use of the slang adjective to these years; a 2017 novel has "Her cake and brownies be bussin'".
Defined on Urban Dictionary as what you say when something is really good.
Spreads online through a trend of photos of food being squeezed hard, often captioned "bussin"; in November a rap song titled "Bussin" is released.
TikTok makes it mainstream with duets and stitches asking "Is it bussin?" on food reviews.

ul: "Is it bussin or nah?" (asking if food is good)
"That new album is bussin, no cap." (beyond food)
"These fries are okay, but the burgers are bussin." (comparing two things)

body: It works mainly as an adjective after "is": the food is bussin. People rarely say "a bussin burger", though you will hear it.

Bussin is casual and enthusiastic. It is everywhere in food videos and among teens, and adults often use it jokingly. It comes from African American English, an origin worth knowing now that the word is used everywhere. It is fine in chats and comments, not in formal writing.

faq.a: It started with food, but now it can mean anything that is really good, like a song, an outfit or a game.
From African American English, probably from "busting" or "bursting". Dictionary.com notes the origin is disputed.
Yes. Saying food or anything else is bussin is strong praise.
